topic: Flattest / lowest country: Maldives — highest natural point about 2.4 m (CIA: 5 m on Vilingili, 8th tee of a golf course), average ground elevation ~1.5 m, 1,190 coral islands in 26 atolls; the Netherlands' highest point Vaalserberg 322 m, Denmark's Møllehøj 171 m; Malé protected by a 3 m sea wall built with Japanese aid after the 1987 floods; 17 October 2009 President Nasheed's cabinet met underwater at Girifushi to sign a declaration ahead of the Copenhagen climate summit.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: The Netherlands is the flattest country — a quarter of it lies below sea level.
myths.reality: Much of the Netherlands is below sea level, but its highest point is 322 m; the Maldives' highest natural point is a few metres and no land rises above about 5 m.

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

screen_exempt: ^A was right|^B was right|^C was right

landscape.our_gap: Clips either tour Maldives resorts or run a 'countries that will disappear' list; nobody puts the three high points side by side, measures the Malé wall against the average and shows the underwater cabinet on a moving map as a quiz.

cia_netherlands.title: Netherlands — Geography
cia_netherlands.notes: highest point Mount Scenery 862 m (Saba); on the European mainland Vaalserberg 322 m; about a quarter of the land below sea level

britannica_maldives.title: Maldives
britannica_maldives.notes: about 1,200 small coral islands; no land higher than about 1.8 m (6 feet) on most islands; capital Malé protected by a sea wall; average elevation about 1.5 m

guardian_cabinet.title: Maldives cabinet makes a splash with underwater meeting
guardian_cabinet.notes: 17 October 2009; President Mohamed Nasheed and 13 ministers in scuba gear 6 m down at Girifushi signed a declaration calling for global emission cuts before the Copenhagen summit

peakbagger_nl.title: Vaalserberg; Møllehøj — country high points
peakbagger_nl.notes: Vaalserberg 322.5 m, highest point of the European Netherlands; Denmark's Møllehøj 170.86 m (surveyed 2005)

bbc_cabinet.title: Maldives cabinet makes a splash
bbc_cabinet.notes: 17 October 2009 underwater cabinet meeting at Girifushi, 4 m down, 30 minutes, declaration signed with waterproof pens ahead of Copenhagen
